predecessors.name: Kievan Rus'
predecessors.text: Pereyaslavl, which Vsevolod I received in Yaroslav's division (Kievan Rus' and Principality of Pereyaslavl pages); Cliopatria's first shape of this state is 1056

successors.name: Mongol Empire
successors.text: the principality's last Cliopatria shape, conquered in March 1239; inside Cliopatria's Mongol Empire shape of 1241

ledger.x: 1054: Yaroslav's death gives Pereyaslavl, with Rostov-Suzdal, to his son Vsevolod I.
1240: Cliopatria's last Pereyaslavl shape; from 1241 the land is inside the Mongol shape.

wars.name: Mongol invasion of Kievan Rus'
wars.outcome: Pereyaslavl is conquered and devastated in March 1239; the land lies empty for generations and Danylo of Halych is met by Tatars at Pereyaslavl in 1245 on his way to Batu Khan.

certainty.note: The steppe frontier on the south and east (Cumans) was never fixed by treaty or survey, and the Dnieper and forest edges are approximate; the page puts the eastern limit only 'not far west from the Seversky Donets'.
